headline: Risk-off premarket reverses Tue rally: oil +3.5% on Amazon data-center strike + Rubio pessimism on ceasefire. NQ -0.57% giving back chip gains ahead of Big Tech quadruple: GOOGL/TSLA/INTC/IBM tonight.
client_frame: Tuesday's roaring session (SPX +0.89%, NDX +1.93%, RUT +1.53%, VIX crushed to 17.05, semis +5.2%, Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%) has partially reversed overnight. Three developments compound: first, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it destroyed the central data infrastructure of AWS ME-South-1 in Bahrain with cruise missiles — the 24th wave of 'Operation Nasr 2', retaliation for the US strike on Iran's Darkhovin nuclear plant Sunday. Amazon, Bahrain and the Pentagon have not confirmed. If verified, this is the second major hit on that facility in five months and the first successful strike on hyperscale cloud infrastructure since the March 1 attack. Second, the US completed its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran and Secretary Rubio said Tehran 'is not serious' about ceasefire — the 10-day truce proposal is now visibly stalled. Third, oil is off to the races again: WTI +3.44% to $87.24, Brent +3.70% to $94.38 in premarket, taking Brent above $92 to a six-week high. The rate market continues to lean hawkish — the 10Y closed 4.628% Tuesday, the highest of the entire conflict period, and 30Y remains above 5%. September FOMC hike odds are now 54.7% (single most likely outcome). Client framing for Wednesday: this is the biggest single earnings day of the quarter setting up into a live oil shock and expanding geopolitical target set. GOOGL, TSLA, INTC and IBM all report after close, with ServiceNow, AT&T and T also on the tape. TSLA at 177x forward earnings has the tightest coil — options-implied move is the biggest for a Tesla print in a year. Alphabet cloud growth and capex commentary is the single most important data point for the AI de-rating question. The reason we are looking at index futures softer this morning is not a change in the earnings thesis — it is that Tuesday's rally left the tape overbought into event risk, and the Amazon-data-center headline is a fresh reminder that Iran's target set has expanded from military to corporate US infrastructure. Sequencing over the next 24 hours matters more than direction: PMI Flash Thu, TSLA/GOOGL tonight, and the FOMC decision one week out. Positioning: hedges paid Tuesday's gap-up; keep them on. Do not chase this bounce into event risk. If Big Tech prints deliver, chip rebound extends and rates likely settle; if they miss, the risk-off tape gets a second leg down and volatility gets bought back aggressively.
